title: Integer Overflow
goal: Learn how Rust handles numeric overflow in debug vs release, and explicit methods.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1: Types and Values

sections.text: Arithmetic with basic operators like `+` and `*` checks for overflow in debug mode. If a calculation exceeds the type limit, the program panics at runtime.

sections.code:
let x: u8 = 255;
// let y = x + 1; // panics in debug!
sections.caption: Basic addition panics on overflow in debug mode.

sections.text: In release mode, standard operators wrap around instead of panicking. To write code that behaves predictably in all builds, use explicit arithmetic methods.

sections.caption: Explicit methods define exact overflow behavior.

sections.text: `saturating_add` stays at the maximum value `u8::MAX`. `wrapping_add` wraps around to zero using modular arithmetic.

sections.caption: overflowing_add returns a tuple with an overflow flag.

sections.text: Error handling with `Option` when operations fail is covered in later decks.

explanation: Learn how Rust handles numeric overflow in debug vs release, and explicit methods.
